I've been working this same land for 20 years. My farm is small — 1.5 mu — but I know it well. Every year it's the same rotation: wheat through winter, maize through summer. My kids work in the city now so the pressure is less than it used to be, but I still want a solid harvest. The well is reliable, so water isn't my worry — it's time and input costs.

**Wheat:** I'll plant in early October after the maize comes off. I use improved variety seed — what the county seed shop carries, usually something like Jimai 22 or similar. I've switched away from keeping my own seed years ago, the yields were never as good. I'll do rotary tillage after maize harvest to break up the stubble, then apply base fertilizer at planting — diammonium phosphate and urea mixed in. I topdress nitrogen at jointing in March. I irrigate three times: once before winter to help roots settle in, once at jointing, once at heading. Two pesticide sprays — one herbicide in winter, one fungicide/insecticide pass before heading. I expect around 450 jin per mu on a decent year.

**Maize:** Right after wheat harvest in June I get the maize in fast — no time to lose. I do rotary tillage to chop up the wheat straw and turn it in. I always buy hybrid seed, that's not a question. I apply fertilizer at planting and topdress once more at the big bell stage. I irrigate twice unless the summer is dry — at silking I'll add a third time if I need to. One herbicide spray early, maybe one more pass for army worm if the village gets hit. I expect around 550-600 jin per mu.
